newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Birch details NZ plan to use SOEs' spare capital.
newsitem.headline: Birch details NZ plan to use SOEs' spare capital.

text.p: New Zealand Finance Minister Bill Birch said on Wednesday that the government, as shareholder in a number of state-owned enterprises (SOEs), planned to recycle any excess capital it deemed to be held in those companies into priority spending on education and health.
"What is important from a shareholder's viewpoint is to strike a good commercial balance between debt and equity," Birch told a hearing of parliament's Finance and Expenditure select committee.
He added that the logic behind the government's review was to place an important commercial discipline on SOE management.
"We would use (the proceeds) to build schools or hospitals," Birch told MPs, adding that in the past the dividend and captial repayments had tended to be used to pay off debt.
He declined to coment on how much the recapitalisation exercise could bring in to government funds.
Treasury officials told the committee that capital structures were being reviewed on a case-by-case basis and it was clear that some had fallen out of line.
However, they also said they could not yet give a "ballpark figure" for the likely proceeds from the exercise.
Birch said although income from SOEs in the past had generally been used "for the repayment of debt, the crown is now faced with a particular demand for capital expenditure".
He noted that the extra capital expenditure this year would amount to NZ$350 million, and the total bill would be $1.5 billion.
Committee member John Wright (Alliance) said his estimate for power company ECNZ was a recapitalisation gain of about $700 million, but neither Birch nor officials would confirm the figure.
